description:
FILED s473t3 (Opus triage of the 79 CATALOG-only blessed rows), on main
d9a2aac0.  PRE-EXISTING.  Probe: scratch/s473t3/probes/p06-sprintf2.pl.

ROW BEHIND IT (baselines/fail-baseline.tsv, 1 row):
  sprintf2.t 1534 (unnamed row; got '0x1.1p+0', expected '0x1.0p+0')
  -- the source is perl-tests/sprintf2.t:844,
     `is(sprintf("%.1a", 1.03125), "0x1.0p+0");`

MEASURED (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    printf("%.1a|%.1a\n", 1.03125, 1.0625)
  perl: 0x1.0p+0|0x1.1p+0
  PCL : 0x1.1p+0|0x1.1p+0
  1.03125 is 0x1.08p+0 -- EXACTLY halfway between 0x1.0 and 0x1.1, so the
  tie rule decides.  1.0625 is 0x1.1p+0 exactly and both agree, which is the
  control that isolates the tie.

MECHANISM: PCL rounds the discarded hex digits half-away-from-zero; C's
`%a` (and therefore perl's) rounds half-to-even.  Fix area: the `(#\a)` arm
of `sprintf-one` in `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp`.

CATALOG NOTE THIS REPLACES: sweep-bug-catalog.md sprintf2.t, "subnormal /
denormal `%a` last-hexdigit rounding" -- this row is the ROUNDING half (a
normal double); #1476 is the subnormal-significand half.

FAMILY: float formatting; siblings #1475, #1476.
subject: BUG (sprintf `%a`): rounding at an EXACT tie goes half-away-from-zero where perl goes half-to-even -- `sprintf "%.1a", 1.03125` (= 0x1.08p+0) is `0x1.0p+0` in perl and `0x1.1p+0` in PCL
